 SpaceX Aims to Be World’s Biggest AI Infrastructure Player in 2027
 Erica Kollmann Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:00 AM CST 5 min read SPCX -4.85%

 Space Exploration Technologies Corp. could become the world's largest AI infrastructure player next year, according to CFO Bret Johnsen , who laid out the company's outlook Tuesday at the TomorrowX Summit during an interview with investor Gavin Baker. 
 Aiming for the Top Spot, Pending Liftoff 
 Johnsen tied the forecast to guidance, saying SpaceX would be "one of, if not the largest player in AI infrastructure" if it meets the targets it has given for next year.

 The longer-term plan leans on orbital computing, with the first orbital compute satellites expected to fly in 2027, the constellation ramping in 2028 and meaningful volume, measured in gigawatts, arriving in 2029. 
 Johnsen described the timeline as his own expectation rather than a figure in the company's filings. 
 Data Centers Prepare for Takeoff 
 Reuters reported in June, citing two people who attended pre-IPO investor presentations led by Johnsen and President Gwynne Shotwell , that SpaceX was aiming to launch initial space-based computing demonstrations by late 2027, ahead of the "as early as 2028" deployment timeline in its IPO filing. 
 Johnsen argued Tuesday that the economics favor orbit over time. "It's really obvious to us," he said, pointing to abundant clean power free of the constraints facing ground-based sites. 
 He expects orbital unit costs to fall with volume and experience while terrestrial costs face growing headwinds. Funding the buildout, he added, will rely largely on the business itself, with payback periods on current contracts typically under a year. 
 "A large portion will be just funded by the business itself," Johnsen said.

 Q3 Numbers Reach New Heights 
 SpaceX's ground-based business is already sizable, with third-quarter revenue up 161% to $14.58 billion, ahead of the consensus estimate of $12.72 billion. 
 The AI unit, which SpaceX calls Super Intelligence, generated $7.56 billion, topping the $5.25 billion from connectivity, and more than $16.4 billion of the $19.6 billion in third-quarter capital spending went to AI. 
 One Customer, Sky-High Share 
 Story Continues A single customer, labeled Customer B in the filing, accounted for 34.5% of third-quarter revenue, and media reports have identified it as Anthropic PBC , although SpaceX has not confirmed the identification. 
 Anthropic agreed earlier this year to take the full capacity of the Colossus 1 data center in Memphis, Tennessee, and Johnsen has described most SpaceX hosting contracts as carrying 90-day terms with a 90-day exit provision, which leaves revenue visibility shorter than a multiyear backlog would. 
 Houston, We Have a Few Hurdles 
 Johnsen has described Starship as the launch vehicle expected to make orbital compute possible, though orbital hardware has yet to fly at scale and spending is heavy. 
 SpaceX will need to deliver on its 2027 guidance for the largest-player claim to hold.

 Building Wealth Across More Than Just the Market 
 Building a resilient portfolio means thinking beyond a single asset or market trend. Economic cycles shift, sectors rise and fall, and no one investment performs well in every environment. That's why many investors look to diversify with platforms that provide access to real estate, fixed-income opportunities, precious metals, and even self-directed retirement accounts. By spreading exposure across multiple asset classes, it becomes easier to manage risk, capture steady returns, and create long-term wealth that isn't tied to the fortunes of just one company or industry. 
 EquityMultiple 
 For accredited investors looking beyond stocks and bonds, EquityMultiple provides access to vetted commercial real estate deals starting at $5,000 , with only ~5% of opportunities passing their due diligence process. 
 Arrived 
 Backed by Jeff Bezos, Arrived Homes makes real estate investing accessible with a low barrier to entry. Investors can buy fractional shares of single-family rentals and vacation homes starting with as little as $100 . This allows everyday investors to diversify into real estate, collect rental income, and build long-term wealth without needing to manage properties directly. 
 Bito 
 As AI coding tools take on more of the work traditionally done by developers, companies are facing new challenges around code quality, context and the rising cost of AI-powered development. Bito is building software designed to help AI coding agents better understand complex codebases while helping companies control AI development costs. Founded by former PubMatic executives, Bito has raised more than $10 million from institutional and individual investors and is now raising additional capital through a Wefunder offering, giving investors an opportunity to invest in a company targeting an emerging need within the rapidly expanding AI software market. 
 FarmTogether 
 Farmland has historically held its value through market volatility and delivered returns uncorrelated to stocks and bonds. For accredited investors, FarmTogether offers direct access to high-quality U.S. farmland starting at $15,000 — fully managed, with no landlord headaches. 
 Fundrise 
 Private real estate and private credit can add income and stability to a stock-heavy portfolio. Fundrise offers access to diversified private real estate and credit strategies through an easy-to-use platform, with professionally managed portfolios designed to generate passive income and long-term growth.
